title: Rebuild perf smoke controller and stable reporting pipeline
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: The current perf smoke runner and post-run reporter are brittle and produce noisy, non-deterministic outputs. This makes triage expensive for regressions and causes false positives during nightly perf regressions. The existing Python controller reuses ad-hoc seeding and homegrown aggregation logic that interacts poorly with our new batching and KV cache experiments.

Goal: Replace the smoke test controller with a small Go service (smokectl) that orchestrates deterministic runs, captures golden artifacts, uploads structured run results to the metrics bucket, and emits a compact HTML+JSON stable-report for engineers and PMs. The new pipeline will: 1) enforce deterministic RNG/temperature seeding per scenario, 2) snapshot model inputs/outputs as golden artifacts for delta diffs, 3) compute bootstrapped confidence intervals to reduce false positives, and 4) retain per-run metadata (kernel selection, sequence length histogram, GPU util) for debugging.

Scope: Implement controller, migrate 12 high-value smoke scenarios, build reporter that produces side-by-side diffs with heuristics (token-level edit distance + semantic embedding similarity threshold), and wire an alert rule for significant regressions to #perf-alerts. Excludes: full migration of synthetic loadgen (follow-up epics).

Why now: Recent flakiness during runtime-1.18->1.19 rollout cost ~3 engineer-days in incident triage. Reducing noise and adding deterministic artifacts will speed future rollouts and make perf alerts actionable.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Marco Chen: Spike completed for deterministic seeding options. Go runtime offers lower tail-latency and we can reuse existing gRPC proto for scenario payloads. Confluence notes: https://confluence.company/revamp-smoke-controller
2025-01-19 - Aisha Kapoor: Prototype smokectl v0.1 runs locally and produces JSON blobs. Observed variability from model side still ~1.5% on short prompts — added bootstrapped CI plan.

2025-01-24 - Code review (PR #5532): request to add schema validation for golden artifacts and reject runs with missing kernel metadata. @Sofia Alvarez requested clearer placement of artifact retention TTL. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/5532

2025-01-30 - Decision: Use 7-day short-term S3 retention for raw artifacts and 90-day long-term compressed archives. Trade-off: short retention reduces storage costs but requires immediate triage on alerts. Documented in design doc.

2025-02-05 - QA: Added fuzz harness to detect non-deterministic seeds on CPU vs GPU. Found two scenarios that diverge due to floating-point kernel ordering; flagged for follow-up with runtime team (ENG-32401).
2025-02-10 - PM feedback (Jamal Reed): Include a condensed HTML summary for PMs with green/yellow/red status and a link to the detailed JSON. Keep summary < 50KB for Slack attachments.
2025-02-12 - Work in progress: Integrating with prometheus-exporter shim and hooking alert rule. Next: migrate remaining 6 scenarios and run 3-night canary.
